results.content: An advanced method for surface damage detection of concrete structures in low-light environments based on image enhancement and object detection networks. # An advanced method for surface damage detection of concrete structures in low-light environments based on image enhancement and object detection networks. To address this challenge, this study proposed a methodology that integrates image enhancement and object detection networks to improve damage identification in such conditions. Specifically, we employ the self-calibrated illumination (SCI) model to reconstruct low-light images, which are then processed by an improved YOLOv5-based network, YOLOv5-GAM-ASFF, incorporating a global attention mechanism (GAM) and adaptive spatial feature fusion (ASFF). Object detection networks constitute one of the most successful models in deep learning, particularly in the domain of image classification tasks (Pan and Li 2022 EPSA-YOLO-V5s: a novel method for detecting the survival rate of rapeseed in a plant factory based on multiple guarantee mechanisms. However, the impact of image degradation in a low-light environments leads to the deterioration of object detection network performance (Shu et al. 2023 Low-light image object detection based on improved YOLOv5 algorithm. The method utilizes a self-calibrating illumination (SCI) module to enhance image quality and subsequently detects damage using the improved YOLOv5-GAM-ASFF. The performance of the YOLOv5s network significantly declines when detecting images captured in low-light environments. To address this issue, data processing techniques are implemented to darken 2483 captured concrete structure damage images, facilitating the training of the YOLOv5-GAM-ASFF network for low-light environment detection. In the preliminary step, high-contrast images are degraded to build a dataset for training image enhancement and object detection networks. The SCI model is used to enhance the quality of low-contrast images, which are then analyzed for surface damage detection using the YOLOv5-GAM-ASFF model. Future studies will look toward developing a real-time damage detection network that integrates object detection and image enhancement modules. * Wu W, Weng J, Zhang P (2022) “URetinex-Net: retinex-based deep unfolding network for low-light image enhancement.” In: 2022 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR). *et al.* An advanced method for surface damage detection of concrete structures in low-light environments based on image enhancement and object detection networks.

results.title: Rapid domain adaptation for disaster impact assessment: Remote sensing of building damage after the 2021 Germany floods - ScienceDirect
results.content: # Rapid domain adaptation for disaster impact assessment: Remote sensing of building damage after the 2021 Germany floods. Systematic progression from semi-supervised to supervised domain adaptation. All adopted techniques significantly improved model performance in a short time, achieving up to 86 % of the potential performance gain compared to supervised learning. The extent of building damage is a crucial indicator for guiding post-disaster relief strategies and rescue operations. However, diverse built environments and variations in imaging setups pose significant challenges for rapid, automated damage assessment from remote sensing data, leading to strong domain shifts and significantly reduced performance of pre-trained models. By employing a Siamese multitask fusion network for semantic segmentation and change detection, we introduce a novel experimental approach that quantifies the influence of a priori information on domain adaptation performance. Up to 86 % of the potential performance gain compared to supervised learning. Semi-supervised domain adaptation, coupled with an automatic labeling strategy based on hazard intensity, provided the highest performance improvements while maintaining low demands on time and human resources.

results.title: Automatic damage detection and evaluation of post-fire reinforced concrete structures using deep learning - ScienceDirect
results.content: # Automatic damage detection and evaluation of post-fire reinforced concrete structures using deep learning. A dual-branch deep network detects both damage type and level in post-fire RC structures with high accuracy. Based on existing damage detection specifications and combined with a deep neural network, an automatic post-fire damage detection and evaluation method for reinforced concrete (RC) components is proposed. Therefore, developing an accurate and efficient method to detect and assess post-fire damage in RC structures is essential. To address these limitations, an infrared thermal image technique for detecting the state of concrete damage was proposed by Wei et al. Recently, damage detection techniques based on deep learning (DL) have emerged, replacing manual feature extraction with Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) which have been effectively used in structural defect detection. However, research on the application of deep learning-based image processing techniques for identifying post-fire surface damage in concrete is scarce. Therefore, in this paper, a multi-branch feature fusion network for automatic damage detection of concrete structures after fire exposure was proposed based on MobileNetv3 and Swin-Transformer block. A post-fire concrete structure detection and assessment scheme suitable for deep learning method was proposed, which is used for dataset division of different damage types and damage levels. A feature fusion network that combines MobileNetv3 and Swin-Transformer block was presented for automatic post-fire RC component damage type and level classification. The related work on deep learning in the field of structural fire damage detection and assessment is discussed in Section 2. In Section 3, a detailed description of the post-fire damage characteristics of RC components is provided, and the related datasets for training and validation of the network are established. Section 4 presents the multi-feature fusion network designed for damage type and damage level classification of post-fire RC components, along with the training and validation strategies. Section 6 introduces both a GUI interface for automated damage detection of post-fire RC components and a separate self-developed smartphone application for damage assessment. Researchers have attempted to introduce deep learning-based image processing techniques into the detection and assessment of concrete damage after fire. This paper presented a multi-branch feature fusion deep network for rapid and automated prediction of damage type and severity in post-fire reinforced concrete components.
